deck: This week highlights vulnerabilities and funding in the space sector.

stories.head: Drones pose new risks to U.S. launches
stories.body: Recent reports indicate that drones are becoming a significant threat to U.S. rocket launch sites, potentially causing millions in delays. This shift underscores that the airspace is not just for rockets, as errant drone flights could disrupt schedules and operations. With the increasing frequency of drone incursions, the industry may need to rethink airspace management strategies.
stories.soWhat: If you thought the only thing to worry about was rocket failures, think again—now we have drones to contend with.

stories.head: EchoStar’s subsidiaries file for Chapter 11
stories.body: EchoStar's satellite TV and wireless subsidiaries have filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, a stark reminder of the financial pressures in the space sector. This move comes as traditional satellite services struggle to compete with streaming and other technologies, raising questions about the viability of legacy players in a rapidly changing market.
stories.soWhat: If legacy companies can’t adapt, expect more of them to follow EchoStar into bankruptcy court.

stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M Series C
stories.body: True Anomaly raised $190 million in a Series C round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding will bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, which are increasingly critical as geopolitical tensions rise. This investment reflects a growing recognition that space security is a necessity, not just a luxury.
stories.soWhat: In a world where threats can come from above, True Anomaly’s success might just be the new norm—if you’re not securing space, you're falling behind.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Blue Origin's New Glenn
watchlist.body: As Blue Origin pushes to return New Glenn to flight, any further delays could impact their credibility in the launch market.

watchlist.title: Watch for Latitude's Oman launch
watchlist.body: Latitude's plan for a 2027 launch from Oman could mark a significant shift in launch geography, depending on execution.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program signals continued government reliance on established players for ground station capabilities.

watchlist.title: Funding trends in defense-tech
watchlist.body: With the defense-tech IPO window showing signs of life, expect increased activity as investors look for the next military unicorn.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
